answer: Cross-epoch behavioural fingerprinting rule. Each identity's action timing, request mix, and interaction graph are hashed into a per-epoch profile; the system checks whether a profile stays within a crystal-clear drift band across epochs, flagging identities whose behaviour jumps abruptly. A new identity on the knoll of its first epochs must behave consistently for several epochs before gaining full weight, so an attacker must run each sybil through slow, costly warm-up cycles. A violet flag marks profiles that fail consistency, freezing their influence.
